Aragonese

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • ciel

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Navarro-Aragonese ciel, cielo, from Latin caelum, from Proto-Italic *kailom, from Proto-Indo-European *keh₂i-lom (“whole”), from *keh₂i-.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈθjelo/
  • IPA(key): /ˈsjelo/ (Benasquese)
  • Syllabification: cie‧lo
  • Rhymes: -elo

Noun

[edit]

cielo m (plural cielos or ciels)

  1. sky
  2. heaven

References

[edit]
  • “cielo”, in Diccionario ortografico de l’aragonés (seguntes la PO de l’EFA)‎[1], Zaragoza: EDACAR, 2023, →ISSN
  • “cielo”, in Ortografía de l’aragonés‎[2], Zaragoza: Academia Aragonesa de la Lengua, 2023, →ISBN

From Latin caelum, from Proto-Italic *kailom, from Proto-Indo-European *keh₂i-lom (“whole”), from *keh₂i-.

Pronunciation

  • Homophone: celo
  • Rhymes: -ɛlo
  • Hyphenation: ciè‧lo

Noun

[edit]

cielo m (plural cieli)

  1. sky
  2. heaven

Related terms

  • celestiale

Descendants

[edit]

  • → Lombard: ciel
  • → Piedmontese: cel

From Old Leonese cielo (compare Asturian cielu and Leonese cielu), from Latin caelum.

Noun

  1. sky
  2. heaven

Old Spanish

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • çielo

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin caelum.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈt͡sjelo/

Noun

[edit]

cielo m (plural cielos)

  1. sky, heavens
    • c. 1250, Alfonso X, Lapidario, f. 77v:
      Et la eſtrella ſiguient delas dos q̃ ſon en el ombro ſinieſtro del boitre uolant a poder en eſta piedra ⁊ della recibe ſu uertud. Et quãdo es en medio cielo, mueſtra eſta piedra mas manifieſta miente ſus obras.
      And the star following the two located in the left elbow of the flying vulture has power over this stone, which draws its virtue from it. And when it is in the center of the sky, this stone more manifestly shows its works.
    • c. 1250, Alfonso X, Lapidario, f. 94r.:
      […] ca todas an uertud et fuerça que reciben de dios por mano delos ſus ang͠ls ⁊ por uertud delos cielos ⁊ delas eſtrellas que en ellos ſon.
      For they all possess a virtue and strength which they receive from God at the hand of his angels and by virtue of the heavens and the stars in them.
  2. (religion) heaven

Synonyms

[edit]
  • (heavens): firmamento m

Descendants

[edit]
  • Ladino: sielo
  • Spanish: cielo
    • → Hiligaynon: sielo
    • → Papiamentu: shelu
    • → Paraguayan Guarani: yvága (“heaven”) (semantic loan)

Spanish

[edit]
Spanish Wikipedia has an article on:
cielo
Wikipedia es

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Spanish cielo, from Latin caelum, from Proto-Italic *kailom, from Proto-Indo-European *keh₂i-lom (“whole”), from *keh₂i-.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈθjelo/ [ˈθje.lo] (Equatorial Guinea, Spain)
  • IPA(key): /ˈsjelo/ [ˈsje.lo] (Latin America, Philippines)
  • Audio (Latin America):(file)
  • Rhymes: -elo
  • Syllabification: cie‧lo

Noun

[edit]

cielo m (plural cielos)

  1. sky
    Synonym: firmamento
  2. heaven
    Synonym: paraíso

  • llovido del cielo
  • mover cielo y tierra
  • orinal del cielo
  • poner el grito en el cielo

Related terms

[edit]
  • celeste
  • celestial
  • célico

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Hiligaynon: sielo
  • → Papiamentu: shelu
  • → Paraguayan Guarani: yvága (“heaven”) (semantic loan)
